atoms.name: natural_succ
atoms.rule: a ↑ is a + 1 for a nonnegative integer; negative inputs give NaN.
atoms.plain: a ↑ is a + 1 for a nonnegative integer; negative inputs give NaN.

atoms.name: natural_pred
atoms.rule: a ↓ is max(0, a - 1) for a nonnegative integer; negative inputs give NaN.
atoms.plain: a ↓ is max(0, a - 1) for a nonnegative integer; negative inputs give NaN.

atoms.name: is_zero
atoms.rule: a ○ is 1 when a is zero and 0 otherwise; negative inputs give NaN.
atoms.plain: a ○ is 1 when a is zero and 0 otherwise; negative inputs give NaN.

domain.en: Values are nonnegative integers. A negative input to an atom gives NaN.

settings.en: The preset that selects these atoms and defaults.
A recursive call unfolds at most this many times; larger counters give NaN.
The range of numbers in generated expressions and branch thresholds.

why.en: These atoms are one example. Atoms are chosen by the user: any function with a rule can be registered and the same three composition forms grow operators from it.

operators.name: △₁
operators.definition: △₁ a = { a ▽₆₀ (▽₃₁ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ▽₆₀ to a and (▽₃₁ a).

operators.name: ♥₂
operators.definition: a ♥₂ b = { 1 ●₂₂ a, if a >= 1 and a < 11 and b >= 5; 0 ♦₁₉, else }
operators.plain: If 1 ≤ a < 11 and b ≥ 5, compute 1 ●₂₂ a; otherwise apply ♦₁₉ to 0.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ☆₃
operators.definition: a ☆₃ b = { b, if a == 0; ((a ↓) ☆₃ b) ♦₁₉, if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with b. Repeat a times (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply ♦₁₉ to the current value.

operators.name: ◆₄
operators.plain: Subtract one from a twice, stopping at zero.

operators.name: ♡₅
operators.plain: Apply ◆₄ to a, then apply ◆₄ to the result.

operators.name: △₆
operators.plain: Apply ♡₅ to a, then subtract one from it, stopping at zero.

operators.name: □₇
operators.plain: Apply ♡₅ to a, then apply ♡₅ to the result.

operators.name: ▽₈
operators.plain: Subtract one from a, stopping at zero, then apply ◆₄ to the result.

operators.name: △₉
operators.plain: Apply △₆ to a, then apply ◆₄ to the result.

operators.name: ●₁₀
operators.plain: Apply ♡₅ to a, then add one to it.

operators.name: ♡₁₁
operators.definition: ♡₁₁ a = { ▽₈ (●₁₀ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ●₁₀ to a, then apply ▽₈ to the result.

operators.name: ▲₁₂
operators.definition: ▲₁₂ a = { (♡₁₁ a) ↑ }
operators.plain: Apply ♡₁₁ to a, then add one to it.

operators.name: ♢₁₃
operators.definition: ♢₁₃ a = { (●₁₀ a) ↑ }
operators.plain: Apply ●₁₀ to a, then add one to it.

operators.name: ★₁₄
operators.definition: ★₁₄ a = { ♢₁₃ (▽₈ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ▽₈ to a, then apply ♢₁₃ to the result.

operators.name: □₁₅
operators.definition: a □₁₅ = { ●₁₀ (●₁₀ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ●₁₀ to a, then apply ●₁₀ to the result.

operators.name: ▽₁₆
operators.definition: ▽₁₆ a = { (♢₁₃ a) ↑ }
operators.plain: Apply ♢₁₃ to a, then add one to it.

operators.name: ♡₁₇
operators.definition: a ♡₁₇ = { ▽₁₆ (a ↓) }
operators.plain: Subtract one from a, stopping at zero, then apply ▽₁₆ to the result.

operators.name: ♠₁₈
operators.definition: ♠₁₈ a = { ▽₁₆ (◆₄ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ◆₄ to a, then apply ▽₁₆ to the result.

operators.name: ♦₁₉
operators.definition: a ♦₁₉ = { (◆₄ a) ♡₁₇ }
operators.plain: Apply ◆₄ to a, then apply ♡₁₇ to the result.

operators.name: ♣₂₀
operators.definition: ♣₂₀ a = { 3 ↑, if a >= 12; a, if a >= 9 and a < 11; a △₆, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 12, add one to 3; otherwise if 9 ≤ a < 11, return a; otherwise apply △₆ to a.

operators.name: ♥₂₁
operators.definition: ♥₂₁ a = { a ♦₁₉, if a >= 10; ♣₂₀ a, if a >= 3 and a < 10; ▽₁₆ a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 10, apply ♦₁₉ to a; otherwise if 3 ≤ a < 10, apply ♣₂₀ to a; otherwise apply ▽₁₆ to a.

operators.name: ●₂₂
operators.definition: a ●₂₂ b = { a □₇, if a >= 8 and b >= 4 and b < 5; △₉ b, if a < 8 and b >= 5 and b < 7; b □₇, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 8 and b ≥ 4 and b < 5, apply □₇ to a; otherwise if a < 8 and b ≥ 5 and b < 7, apply △₉ to b; otherwise apply □₇ to b.

operators.name: ♠₂₃
operators.definition: a ♠₂₃ = { ▲₁₂ a, if a >= 3 and a < 10; ▽₈ 0, else }
operators.plain: If 3 ≤ a < 10, apply ▲₁₂ to a; otherwise apply ▽₈ to 0.

operators.name: ♡₂₄
operators.definition: a ♡₂₄ b = { b □₇, if a >= 7 and b >= 10 and b < 11; a ●₂₂ b, if a >= 7 and b >= 3 and b < 5; a ♥₂ b, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 7 and b ≥ 10 and b < 11, apply □₇ to b; otherwise if a ≥ 7 and b ≥ 3 and b < 5, compute a ●₂₂ b; otherwise compute a ♥₂ b.

operators.name: ♧₂₅
operators.definition: ♧₂₅ a = { a ↓, if a < 4; 0 ♥₂ a, if a >= 8 and a < 12; 3 ♡₂₄ a, else }
operators.plain: If a < 4, subtract one from a, stopping at zero; otherwise if 8 ≤ a < 12, compute 0 ♥₂ a; otherwise compute 3 ♡₂₄ a.

operators.name: ◇₂₆
operators.definition: a ◇₂₆ b = { a ●₂₂ (▽₈ b), if a >= 12 and b >= 3 and b < 6; (●₁₀ b) ●₂₂ a, if a < 10 and b >= 3 and b < 6; a ♥₂ 5, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 12 and b ≥ 3 and b < 6, apply ●₂₂ to a and (▽₈ b); otherwise if a < 10 and b ≥ 3 and b < 6, apply ●₁₀ to b, then apply ●₂₂ to the result and a; otherwise compute a ♥₂ 5.

operators.name: ●₂₇
operators.definition: a ●₂₇ = { a ♥₂ a, if a >= 3; a ◇₂₆ a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 3, compute a ♥₂ a; otherwise compute a ◇₂₆ a.

operators.name: ■₂₈
operators.definition: a ■₂₈ b = { ♢₁₃ 8, if a >= 11 and b < 5; b ♥₂ a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 11 and b < 5, apply ♢₁₃ to 8; otherwise compute b ♥₂ a.

operators.name: ●₂₉
operators.definition: a ●₂₉ b = { ♧₂₅ 6, if a >= 5 and a < 7 and b >= 6; b ♡₂₄ b, if a >= 7 and a < 10 and b < 3; ♥₂₁ a, else }
operators.plain: If 5 ≤ a < 7 and b ≥ 6, apply ♧₂₅ to 6; otherwise if 7 ≤ a < 10 and b < 3, compute b ♡₂₄ b; otherwise apply ♥₂₁ to a.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: □₃₀
operators.definition: a □₃₀ b = { (♠₁₈ b) ♡₂₄ (△₉ 0), if a >= 6 and a < 9 and b < 1; (a ↓) ♡₂₄ b, if a < 4 and b < 1; ●₁₀ (b ●₂₂ a), else }
operators.plain: Chooses between 3 cases by testing a and b; the cases combine △₉, ●₂₂, ●₁₀, ♠₁₈, ♡₂₄ and ↓.

operators.name: ▽₃₁
operators.definition: ▽₃₁ a = { (♠₁₈ a) ●₂₉ (♡₅ a), if a >= 11; (a △₆) ◇₂₆ (♣₂₀ 4), if a >= 6 and a < 11; ▲₁₂ (a ◇₂₆ a), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 11, apply ♠₁₈ to a, then apply ●₂₉ to the result and (♡₅ a); otherwise if 6 ≤ a < 11, apply △₆ to a, then apply ◇₂₆ to the result and (♣₂₀ 4); otherwise apply ◇₂₆ to a and a, then apply ▲₁₂ to the result.

operators.name: □₃₂
operators.definition: a □₃₂ b = { (△₉ b) ■₂₈ (▽₈ a) }
operators.plain: Apply △₉ to b, then apply ■₂₈ to the result and (▽₈ a).

operators.name: ▲₃₃
operators.definition: ▲₃₃ a = { a □₇, if a >= 7; a ♡₂₄ 0, if a >= 1 and a < 4; a ◇₂₆ a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 7, apply □₇ to a; otherwise if 1 ≤ a < 4, compute a ♡₂₄ 0; otherwise compute a ◇₂₆ a.

operators.name: ▲₃₄
operators.definition: a ▲₃₄ b = { (♥₂₁ a) ●₂₉ b }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₂₁ to a, then apply ●₂₉ to the result and b.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ●₃₅
operators.definition: a ●₃₅ = { a □₃₀ a }
operators.plain: Compute a □₃₀ a.

operators.name: ▲₃₆
operators.definition: a ▲₃₆ b = { (●₁₀ a) ▲₃₄ (▲₁₂ b) }
operators.plain: Apply ●₁₀ to a, then apply ▲₃₄ to the result and (▲₁₂ b).

operators.name: ◇₃₇
operators.definition: a ◇₃₇ b = { b, if a >= 12 and b >= 9; (▲₁₂ 2) ●₂₉ (▲₁₂ a), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 12 and b ≥ 9, return b; otherwise apply ▲₁₂ to 2, then apply ●₂₉ to the result and (▲₁₂ a).

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ♧₃₈
operators.definition: a ♧₃₈ = { a ▲₃₄ a }
operators.plain: Compute a ▲₃₄ a.

operators.name: ♣₃₉
operators.definition: a ♣₃₉ b = { a ♡₂₄ (▲₃₃ b) }
operators.plain: Apply ♡₂₄ to a and (▲₃₃ b).

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order and negation

operators.name: ♡₄₀
operators.definition: ♡₄₀ a = { (♡₅ a) ▲₃₄ (★₁₄ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♡₅ to a, then apply ▲₃₄ to the result and (★₁₄ a).

operators.name: ●₄₁
operators.definition: a ●₄₁ = { (♠₁₈ a) ♣₃₉ (a ↓), if a >= 8; (▲₃₃ a) □₃₀ (▽₁₆ a), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 8, apply ♠₁₈ to a, then apply ♣₃₉ to the result and (a ↓); otherwise apply ▲₃₃ to a, then apply □₃₀ to the result and (▽₁₆ a).

operators.name: ♣₄₂
operators.definition: a ♣₄₂ b = { (3 ♣₃₉ a) ♦₁₉, if a >= 7 and b >= 0 and b < 1; ♥₂₁ (b ◇₃₇ b), if a < 7 and b >= 3 and b < 11; b, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 7 and b ≥ 0 and b < 1, apply ♣₃₉ to 3 and a, then apply ♦₁₉ to the result; otherwise if a < 7 and b ≥ 3 and b < 11, apply ◇₃₇ to b and b, then apply ♥₂₁ to the result; otherwise return b.

operators.name: ●₄₃
operators.definition: a ●₄₃ b = { 0, if a == 0; ((a ↓) ●₄₃ b) ◇₃₇ a, if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): when a = 0 the result is 0; otherwise let r be the result for a ↓, then apply ◇₃₇ to r and a.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ♠₄₄
operators.definition: a ♠₄₄ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♠₄₄ (b ↓)) □₇, if b > 0 and b <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat b times (for b from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply □₇ to the current value.

operators.name: ◇₄₅
operators.definition: ◇₄₅ a = { a, if a == 0; a ▲₃₄ (◇₄₅ (a ↓)), if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): when a = 0 the result is a; otherwise let r be the result for a ↓, then replace r by a ▲₃₄ r.

operators.name: ☆₄₆
operators.definition: ☆₄₆ a = { a, if a == 0; ▽₁₆ (☆₄₆ (a ↓)), if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with 0. Repeat a times (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply ▽₁₆ to the current value.

operators.name: △₄₇
operators.definition: a △₄₇ = { 0, if a == 0; ((a ↓) △₄₇) ●₃₅, if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with 0. Repeat a times (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply ●₃₅ to the current value.

operators.name: □₄₈
operators.definition: a □₄₈ = { 0, if a == 0; ((a ↓) □₄₈) □₁₅, if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with 0. Repeat a times (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply □₁₅ to the current value.

operators.name: ♡₄₉
operators.definition: a ♡₄₉ b = { b, if a == 0; ((a ↓) ♡₄₉ b) ♠₂₃, if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with b. Repeat a times (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply ♠₂₃ to the current value.

operators.name: ●₅₀
operators.definition: a ●₅₀ b = { b, if a == 0; ♧₂₅ ((a ↓) ●₅₀ b), if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with b. Repeat a times (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply ♧₂₅ to the current value.

operators.name: ♦₅₁
operators.definition: a ♦₅₁ = { 0, if a == 0; ((a ↓) ♦₅₁) ◇₂₆ ((a ↓) ♦₅₁), if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with 0. Repeat a times (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply ◇₂₆ to the current value and the current value.

operators.name: ♠₅₂
operators.definition: a ♠₅₂ = { (a △₄₇) ♡₄₉ (★₁₄ a) }
operators.plain: Apply △₄₇ to a, then apply ♡₄₉ to the result and (★₁₄ a).

operators.name: ♥₅₃
operators.definition: a ♥₅₃ b = { (♥₂₁ b) ●₄₃ (△₉ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₂₁ to b, then apply ●₄₃ to the result and (△₉ a).

operators.name: ♠₅₄
operators.definition: a ♠₅₄ = { (♡₅ a) ☆₃ a }
operators.plain: Apply ♡₅ to a, then apply ☆₃ to the result and a.

operators.name: ♠₅₅
operators.definition: a ♠₅₅ = { (▽₃₁ a) △₄₇ }
operators.plain: Apply ▽₃₁ to a, then apply △₄₇ to the result.

operators.name: ♧₅₆
operators.definition: ♧₅₆ a = { a ▲₃₄ (◇₄₅ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ▲₃₄ to a and (◇₄₅ a).

operators.name: ♣₅₇
operators.definition: a ♣₅₇ = { ☆₄₆ (△₉ a) }
operators.plain: Apply △₉ to a, then apply ☆₄₆ to the result.

operators.name: ♣₅₈
operators.definition: a ♣₅₈ b = { (b ♦₅₁) ●₄₃ (▽₁₆ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♦₅₁ to b, then apply ●₄₃ to the result and (▽₁₆ a).

operators.name: ♥₅₉
operators.definition: a ♥₅₉ = { 8 ♥₅₃ a }

operators.name: ▽₆₀
operators.definition: a ▽₆₀ b = { (♡₁₁ b) ●₅₀ a }
operators.plain: Apply ♡₁₁ to b, then apply ●₅₀ to the result and a.

operators.name: ◇₆₁
operators.definition: ◇₆₁ a = { (♥₂₁ a) ♡₄₉ (▽₃₁ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♥₂₁ to a, then apply ♡₄₉ to the result and (▽₃₁ a).

operators.name: ●₆₂

operators.name: ♥₆₃
operators.definition: a ♥₆₃ b = { (▽₃₁ b) ▽₆₀ (a ♦₁₉) }

operators.name: ♤₆₄
operators.definition: ♤₆₄ a = { (a □₁₅) ♡₄₉ (♧₂₅ a) }
operators.plain: Apply □₁₅ to a, then apply ♡₄₉ to the result and (♧₂₅ a).

operators.name: ■₆₅
operators.definition: a ■₆₅ b = { (b ♣₅₇) ♠₄₄ (♡₅ a) }

operators.name: △₆₆
operators.definition: a △₆₆ = { (♥₂₁ a) ■₆₅ (a △₆), if a >= 2 and a < 10; a □₃₀ (△₁ a), if a >= 1 and a < 2; △₉ (a ●₄₃ a), else }
operators.plain: If 2 ≤ a < 10, apply ♥₂₁ to a, then apply ■₆₅ to the result and (a △₆); otherwise if 1 ≤ a < 2, apply □₃₀ to a and (△₁ a); otherwise apply ●₄₃ to a and a, then apply △₉ to the result.

operators.name: ♧₆₇
operators.definition: a ♧₆₇ b = { (♧₂₅ b) ●₄₃ a, if a < 2 and b >= 9; (♡₅ a) ♥₅₃ a, else }
operators.plain: If a < 2 and b ≥ 9, apply ♧₂₅ to b, then apply ●₄₃ to the result and a; otherwise apply ♡₅ to a, then apply ♥₅₃ to the result and a.

operators.name: ♥₆₈
operators.definition: a ♥₆₈ b = { (◇₄₅ b) ◇₂₆ (♣₂₀ 2), if a < 7 and b >= 12; (●₁₀ 2) ♡₄₉ a, else }
operators.plain: If a < 7 and b ≥ 12, apply ◇₄₅ to b, then apply ◇₂₆ to the result and (♣₂₀ 2); otherwise apply ●₁₀ to 2, then apply ♡₄₉ to the result and a.

operators.name: ▼₆₉
operators.definition: a ▼₆₉ = { a ♦₅₁, if a >= 10; ◆₄ a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 10, apply ♦₅₁ to a; otherwise apply ◆₄ to a.

operators.name: ♠₇₀
operators.definition: ♠₇₀ a = { (◇₆₁ a) ▲₃₆ (3 ♦₅₁), if a >= 12; a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 12, apply ◇₆₁ to a, then apply ▲₃₆ to the result and (3 ♦₅₁); otherwise return a.

operators.name: ♠₇₁
operators.definition: a ♠₇₁ = { (♠₇₀ a) ♧₆₇ a, if a >= 5 and a < 10; (a △₄₇) ♥₆₃ (a △₄₇), if a >= 10; a ▽₆₀ (△₉ a), else }
operators.plain: If 5 ≤ a < 10, apply ♠₇₀ to a, then apply ♧₆₇ to the result and a; otherwise if a ≥ 10, apply △₄₇ to a, then apply ♥₆₃ to the result and (itself); otherwise apply ▽₆₀ to a and (△₉ a).

operators.name: ☆₇₂
operators.definition: ☆₇₂ a = { 0 ●₆₂ a, if a < 2; a △₆₆, else }
operators.plain: If a < 2, compute 0 ●₆₂ a; otherwise apply △₆₆ to a.

operators.name: ♢₇₃
operators.definition: a ♢₇₃ = { a ●₄₃ 0, if a >= 8; a ■₂₈ a, if a >= 3 and a < 7; 4 ☆₃ a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 8, compute a ●₄₃ 0; otherwise if 3 ≤ a < 7, compute a ■₂₈ a; otherwise compute 4 ☆₃ a.

operators.name: ■₇₄
operators.definition: a ■₇₄ = { ♡₁₁ (♧₂₅ 1), if a >= 11; (△₁ a) ☆₃ a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 11, apply ♧₂₅ to 1, then apply ♡₁₁ to the result; otherwise apply △₁ to a, then apply ☆₃ to the result and a.

operators.name: ♥₇₅
operators.definition: a ♥₇₅ = { a, if a >= 0 and a < 6; (☆₄₆ 2) ▽₆₀ (♢₁₃ a), else }
operators.plain: If 0 ≤ a < 6, return a; otherwise apply ☆₄₆ to 2, then apply ▽₆₀ to the result and (♢₁₃ a).

operators.name: ◇₇₆
operators.definition: ◇₇₆ a = { 0, if a == 0; a ♠₄₄ (◇₇₆ (a ↓)), if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): when a = 0 the result is 0; otherwise let r be the result for a ↓, then replace r by a ♠₄₄ r.

operators.name: ★₇₇
operators.definition: a ★₇₇ b = { b, if a == 0; ♧₅₆ ((a ↓) ★₇₇ b), if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with b. Repeat a times (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply ♧₅₆ to the current value.

interest.nearest_transform: behavioural duplicate up to argument order

operators.name: ▲₇₈
operators.definition: a ▲₇₈ b = { b, if a == 0; a ■₆₅ ((a ↓) ▲₇₈ b), if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Recurse on a (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): when a = 0 the result is b; otherwise let r be the result for a ↓, then replace r by a ■₆₅ r.

operators.name: ●₇₉
operators.definition: a ●₇₉ = { 0, if a == 0; ((a ↓) ●₇₉) ♠₅₂, if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with 0. Repeat a times (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply ♠₅₂ to the current value.

operators.name: ♤₈₀
operators.definition: a ♤₈₀ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ♤₈₀ (b ↓)) ■₆₅ a, if b > 0 and b <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat b times (for b from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply ■₆₅ to the current value and a.

operators.name: ▲₈₁
operators.definition: a ▲₈₁ b = { b, if a == 0; ((a ↓) ▲₈₁ b) △₆₆, if a > 0 and a <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with b. Repeat a times (for a from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply △₆₆ to the current value.

operators.name: ☆₈₂
operators.definition: a ☆₈₂ b = { a, if b == 0; ☆₇₂ (a ☆₈₂ (b ↓)), if b > 0 and b <= 5 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat b times (for b from 0 to 5; other values give NaN): apply ☆₇₂ to the current value.

operators.name: ♡₈₃
operators.definition: a ♡₈₃ b = { (b □₁₅) ★₇₇ (△₁ a) }
operators.plain: Apply □₁₅ to b, then apply ★₇₇ to the result and (△₁ a).

operators.name: ♥₈₄
operators.definition: ♥₈₄ a = { a ▲₈₁ a }
operators.plain: Compute a ▲₈₁ a.

operators.name: ♢₈₅
operators.definition: a ♢₈₅ = { (a ♢₇₃) ▲₇₈ (♠₁₈ a) }
operators.plain: Apply ♢₇₃ to a, then apply ▲₇₈ to the result and (♠₁₈ a).

operators.name: □₈₆
operators.definition: a □₈₆ = { a ♠₄₄ (a ♢₈₅) }
operators.plain: Apply ♠₄₄ to a and (a ♢₈₅).

operators.name: ☆₈₇
operators.definition: a ☆₈₇ b = { (♧₅₆ b) ▲₇₈ a }
operators.plain: Apply ♧₅₆ to b, then apply ▲₇₈ to the result and a.

operators.name: ▲₈₈
operators.definition: a ▲₈₈ b = { (a ■₇₄) ☆₈₇ (▲₁₂ b) }
operators.plain: Apply ■₇₄ to a, then apply ☆₈₇ to the result and (▲₁₂ b).

operators.name: ♧₈₉
operators.definition: a ♧₈₉ b = { (a ♣₄₂ b) □₈₆ }
operators.plain: Apply ♣₄₂ to a and b, then apply □₈₆ to the result.

operators.name: ♣₉₀
operators.definition: a ♣₉₀ b = { (★₁₄ a) ★₇₇ (♡₁₁ b) }
operators.plain: Apply ★₁₄ to a, then apply ★₇₇ to the result and (♡₁₁ b).

operators.name: ▽₉₁
operators.definition: a ▽₉₁ b = { (♡₄₀ a) ▲₈₁ (▽₈ b) }
operators.plain: Apply ♡₄₀ to a, then apply ▲₈₁ to the result and (▽₈ b).

operators.name: ♤₉₂
operators.definition: a ♤₉₂ = { 9 ♧₈₉ a }

operators.name: ♥₉₃
operators.definition: a ♥₉₃ = { (a ●₆₂ a) □₈₆ }
operators.plain: Apply ●₆₂ to a and a, then apply □₈₆ to the result.

operators.name: ♣₉₄
operators.definition: a ♣₉₄ b = { a ◇₃₇ b, if a < 7 and b < 7; 8 ♤₈₀ b, if a >= 7 and a < 8 and b >= 7 and b < 8; 2 ♥₆₃ b, else }
operators.plain: If a < 7 and b < 7, compute a ◇₃₇ b; otherwise if 7 ≤ a < 8 and b ≥ 7 and b < 8, compute 8 ♤₈₀ b; otherwise compute 2 ♥₆₃ b.

operators.name: ▽₉₅
operators.definition: a ▽₉₅ b = { a ♡₈₃ 2, if a >= 12 and b >= 9; a ♣₃₉ a, if a >= 1 and a < 12 and b < 6; ♡₁₁ 4, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 12 and b ≥ 9, compute a ♡₈₃ 2; otherwise if 1 ≤ a < 12 and b < 6, compute a ♣₃₉ a; otherwise apply ♡₁₁ to 4.

operators.name: ◇₉₆
operators.definition: a ◇₉₆ b = { b ♤₈₀ (▲₁₂ b), if a >= 7 and b >= 7; ♠₇₀ (1 ♡₈₃ b), else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 7 and b ≥ 7, apply ♤₈₀ to b and (▲₁₂ b); otherwise apply ♡₈₃ to 1 and b, then apply ♠₇₀ to the result.

operators.name: ■₉₇
operators.definition: a ■₉₇ b = { (b ●₂₇) ♣₉₄ a, if a >= 10 and b >= 12; a, else }
operators.plain: If a ≥ 10 and b ≥ 12, apply ●₂₇ to b, then apply ♣₉₄ to the result and a; otherwise return a.

operators.name: △₉₈
operators.definition: △₉₈ a = { (a ♢₈₅) ♥₂ (a ♠₅₄), if a >= 11; ◇₆₁ (a ●₃₅), if a >= 4 and a < 11; (♡₅ a) ☆₃ (●₁₀ 1), else }

operators.name: □₉₉
operators.definition: a □₉₉ = { ♢₁₃ 8, if a < 9; a ▲₈₈ a, else }
operators.plain: If a < 9, apply ♢₁₃ to 8; otherwise compute a ▲₈₈ a.

operators.name: □₁₀₀
operators.definition: a □₁₀₀ = { ♥₈₄ (a ♥₅₃ a), if a < 7; a ♣₉₄ (a ○), if a >= 7 and a < 10; (♥₈₄ a) ♥₆₃ (♢₁₃ 2), else }
operators.plain: If a < 7, apply ♥₅₃ to a and a, then apply ♥₈₄ to the result; otherwise if 7 ≤ a < 10, apply ♣₉₄ to a and (1 if a is zero and 0 otherwise); otherwise apply ♥₈₄ to a, then apply ♥₆₃ to the result and (♢₁₃ 2).
